newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar ranged on slow buys, offtake hopes.
newsitem.headline: India sugar ranged on slow buys, offtake hopes.

text.p: Sugar prices held steady in a narrow band on the local market on Monday, dealers said.
Consumer buying remained slow despite the approaching festival season but local stockists were reserved sellers as they expect higher offtake in the next few days.

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 was steady at 1,477/1,508 rupees per quintal as was sugar M-30 at 1,501/1,535 rupees per quintal. Limited offerings by millers also kept inflow of sugar from mills to the market at a low ebb.

Sugar mill delivery remained subdued amid sluggish outstation buying. In the mill delivery, sugar S-30 fell by five rupees at 1,410/1,420 rupees per quintal while M-30 slid by the same margin at 1,435/1,450 rupees per quintal.
"Free sale quota for August is 750,000 tonnes. This quantity is not sufficient for the current month, looking at the approaching series of Hindu festivals," one broker said.
"Sentiment is firm at the close and I am expecting prices to go up in coming days on festival buying," he added.
The free sale quota for July was 750,000 tonnes against 800,000 tonnes released for June.
